Subject: Dedicated capacity guidance - 70B model, mixed 8k/32k windows\n
Hi Vanessa,\n
We're ramping our pilot with a 70B open model (custom fine-tune) and expect a mixed workload: ~60% of calls will be short (<= 8k tokens), 40% long-form (up to 32k). Target steady-state: 1200 QPS peak with median request length ~800 tokens, but long jobs will produce bursts (batch of 40–60 concurrent long sessions).\n
Attached is a small model profile (kernelfit_model_profile.csv) showing parameter count / avg seq length in eval logs. Can you give a ballpark for committed dedicated capacity (A100-80 style) and how much quantization will help (we can tolerate minor accuracy loss if it reduces capex)? Specifically:\n
- Baseline GPU count for fp16 serving with 70B and a 32k KV cache workload\n- How much memory is the KV cache for 32k vs 8k in practice (per concurrent session)\n- If we go to 8-bit or 4-bit quant, how does that change the required GPUs and the operational tradeoffs?\n
We have procurement timelines (~45d) so need an estimate to include in the SOW.\n
Thanks — Daria\n
--

To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kernelfit sizing + quant tradeoffs (internal)\n
Folks — summary from Daria's ask (attached profile): 70B fine-tune, mixed 8k/32k traffic, target steady 1200 qps with 40 concurrent long sessions during bursts. Procurement needs a committed count in ~45d.\n
Assumptions we used below: fp16 weights = ~140 GB (70B * 2 bytes), KV stored in fp16 => KV cache scales with seq_len. For our reference 70B architecture (LLM-like):\n- KV cache per token (rough estimate): ~0.00075 GB/token (0.75 MB/token) for the whole model at fp16;\n  - 8k window => ~6 GB per concurrent session (8,000 * 0.00075)\n  - 32k window => ~24 GB per concurrent session (32,000 * 0.00075)\n
Notes: quantization primarily shrinks model weight footprint, not KV cache (activations/KV remain fp16/bf16 unless we explicitly offload or quantize KV which carries accuracy/perf risk).\n
Sizing sketches (back-of-envelope):\nOption A — conservative (no quantization, fp16 weights):\n- Model weight: ~140 GB (split across GPUs) -> requires multi-GPU placement (sharded or tensor parallelism).\n- Typical approach: 2x A100-80 for model shards + capacity for KV/headroom. For 40 concurrent long sessions (32k) KV alone = 40 * 24 GB = 960 GB (too large to keep fully on GPU). So pure in-GPU KV for long windows is infeasible without streaming/offload.\n- Recommendation: avoid committing pure fp16-only pool for 32k-heavy workload. Use hybrid NVMe/KV offload + additional headroom.\n
Option B — aggressive quant (q4_0 / q4_1) + NVMe offload for KV:
- Quantized weight size: ~35–40 GB (4-bit representation + packing/aux) for 70B -> fits on a single 80 GB GPU with room for runtime tensors, but KV still needs ~24 GB per long session (fp16).\n- With NVMe-backed KV streaming we can serve long-context sessions while keeping model on one GPU. Operationally this allows higher density: ~6–8 long sessions per 80GB GPU before NVMe latency degrades tail latency.\n- For the customer mix (60% short, 40% long bursts): estimate effective density per 80GB GPU: ~40–60 short sessions (8k or less) OR ~6 long sessions (32k) if NVMe-backed.\n
Production committed pool estimate (targeting 99th latency SLO 1.5s for short calls, 95th for long calls):\n- If we require fp16+in-GPU KV for short-heavy (no offload): ~20 x A100-80 (very conservative, large and expensive).\n- If we accept q4_0 + KV offload NVMe + intelligent routing (route long sessions to a pool optimized for offload): ~6–9 x A100-80 committed to start. This includes headroom for burst scaling and reserved throughput.\n
Tradeoffs and recommended path:\n1) Start with q4_0 quantized model in a dedicated pool with NVMe-backed KV offload for long sessions. This minimizes committed GPU count and is implementable within the procurement window.\2) Provide per-route routing: short calls served from an in-GPU hot pool (higher density), long calls routed to offload-enabled nodes.\3) Add a small warm standby (1–2 GPUs) for failover and canary/pin deployments.\
Action items: Priyom — can you validate the density numbers above with a quick micro-bench using our q4 runtime? Marcus/Neha — assuming Priyom confirms, I can produce a committed-capacity figure and a simple run-rate cost delta for SOW.\n
Attachments: kv_cache_sizing.xlsx (worked example), draft SOW in the external reply.\n
Thanks,\nVanessa\n

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity guidance - memory/windowing & quantization (Kernelfit)\n
Hi Daria / Carlos — following our internal sizing pass, here's a short, procurement-ready summary you can include in the SOW. Priyom is copied for technical follow-up.\n
Executive recommendation (committed reserved pool):\n- Initial committed pool: 8 x A100-80 reserved (region: us-west). Rationale: q4_0 quantized weights + NVMe-backed KV offload for long windows balances cost and latency headroom for your stated traffic mix.\n- Routing policy: route <=8k sessions to a hot in-GPU pool (higher density), route 32k sessions to offload-enabled nodes.\n- Expected density (estimates): short sessions: ~45–60 concurrent per GPU; long sessions (32k) with NVMe offload: ~6 concurrent per GPU.\n- Why not fp16-only? FP16 weights (~140 GB) with full in-GPU KV for long windows would require an order-of-magnitude more GPUs and NVMe offload is necessary for 32k workloads.\n
Quantization impact:\n- q8/int8: ~2x weight reduction, modest accuracy change. Good middle ground.\n- q4_0: ~3–4x weight reduction, largest cost savings; small but non-zero accuracy delta. We recommend q4_0 for the committed pool and a small percentage of inference routed to a higher-precision canary for live quality checks.\n
Next steps / ask from Kernelfit team:\n1) Confirm acceptance of q4_0 as default for committed pool (we'll include fallback routes/quality monitors in SOW).\2) Provide a short list of 8–12 representative prompts (we'll run internal evals against q4_0 and q8).\3) If procurement needs an fp16-only option, we can price that as an upsell but it will materially increase committed GPU counts.\n
Attachments: redwood_dedicated_sow_v1.docx (SOW options), kv_cache_sizing.xlsx (worked example). Drive folder with sizing artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_kernelfit-sizing\n
